title: a16z picks for one world-class strength, not absence of weaknesses
dek: Horowitz argues that every great founder has fatal flaws, but if they possess one world-class ability, all other deficits should be ignored—this is a16z's core founder evaluation principle.
why: Rare to hear Horowitz explain a16z's founding purpose, his methodology for identifying founders, and his genuine shift in thinking as AI disrupts SaaS consumption habits.
who: Founders assessing their investment potential, investors learning to spot talent, and professionals trying to understand whether AI is a bubble.
skip: The opening Kanye recording studio anecdote and hip-hop battle stories can be skipped without losing the business insights.

points.h: Build products for founders, not limited partners
points.body: Horowitz says traditional VCs excel at making money for LPs and picking winners, but teach founders nothing about becoming CEO. a16z's founding premise inverted this: use management fees to build platforms that help founders hire, access networks, and handle regulatory issues. The firm becomes a network—CEO barbecues give founders the feeling they could actually reach Mark Zuckerberg or Larry Page.

points.h: Founder's one world-class strength outweighs all other weaknesses
points.body: The investment decision hinges on a single question: does this founder have one ability that ranks first in the world? If yes, all other shortcomings become irrelevant. Horowitz cites Elon as proof—his personality has serious flaws, but his core ability is so dominant that no pressure can shake it. That's the bet worth making.

points.h: When Biden excluded them, Silicon Valley chose Trump
points.body: a16z fought the Biden administration on two fronts: crypto enterprises were kicked out of the banking system on shaky legal grounds and received questionable Wells notices; a final executive order demanded government pre-approval for GPU sales—effectively locking them out of AI competition at the chip level. But the real breaking point was complete access denial: Horowitz couldn't secure a single meeting with Biden officials, even after calls to Google's Sundar, Eli Lilly's Dave Ricks, and Apple's Tim Cook in four years.

points.h: Wrong hiring criteria systematically exclude talented people
points.body: When Chris Lyons interviewed at a16z, the hiring manager—from investment banking—evaluated him against banking standards for what was fundamentally a relationship role. Horowitz reframed the filter to ‘world-class relationship talent’ and hired him. Lyons was promoted eight times afterward. If they'd stuck with the original criteria, his race might have prevented advancement because no one would understand why he was hired in the first place.

points.h: AI is computing reinvented in compressed time, not a sector fad
points.body: Horowitz rejects treating AI like crypto—as a ‘sector bubble’. What's actually happening is the entire computing industry being reinvented in two years, compressing what took eighty years with greater impact. His benchmark is straightforward: any problem you believed could be solved is now actually being solved. Traffic deaths fall because of Waymo. Cancer is being genuinely attacked.

points.h: Today's AI growth trajectory breaks from the dot-com pattern
points.body: When the dot-com bubble burst, only 50–60 million people were online globally, half on dial-up—not enough users to justify valuations. Token prices now drop approximately 100x annually. Consumer adoption rates are the fastest in history. Claims that chip demand is artificially inflated miss the point: Nvidia can't manufacture enough to meet real demand. The actual bottleneck will be power and cooling.

points.h: LLMs are making custom software cheaper than annual subscriptions
points.body: Horowitz switched to Cursor, then ChatGPT, then Claude Code. Within days of using Claude Code he cancelled HubSpot and wrote his own CRM. A week later he dropped Affinity and built his own fundraising platform. He now calculates: is this $400-a-month subscription worth it, or can I build something better in four days? This is why SaaS valuations are depressed—even individual users can rebuild your product on someone else's GPU.

points.h: AI infrastructure is stuck in an immature architecture phase
points.body: Horowitz predicts the next 8–12 months will see wholesale reinvention of AI infrastructure, mirroring early cloud computing when everyone thought ‘just move software to the cloud’ would work—it didn't. Storage, networking, operating systems, virtualization, containers all had to be rebuilt. Now processing a single AI request can take a full week with no matching system layer. Nvidia chips designed for gaming waste power and suffer low yields. Even feeding all internet data into training might not be the endgame.

terms.def: Measuring an individual's impact by the subsequent achievements of people they trained, analogous to how NFL coaching legacies are evaluated.
